A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 20 readable pages and complete Appendices A-K. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to version/date markings and one table-label punctuation correction.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and search experiments across four domains in Section 4, Figure 2, and Tables 1-2, supplemented by ablations and training results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments, including the appendix sensitivity analyses and complete training results in Table 8.

M1.justification: The clustering-based, heuristic-based, and hybrid rerooters in Section 3 are unchanged, as are their weight formulas and Algorithms 1-3 in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BoulderDash, CraftWorld, Sokoban, and gridworld TSP, including the same BoulderDash dirt-density scenarios. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline membership: LTS, LTS(πSG), PHS*(πSG), and WA*(1.5) in the main comparisons, and PHS*(πSG) in the complexity-scaling comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D retain identical splits, bootstrap procedures, training limits, model configurations, and evaluation metrics, including the 512,000-expansion test budget.

E4.justification: Appendices E-I retain the same analyses of clustering level, graph-update frequency, rerooter balance, heuristic temperature, and cluster separation. The complexity-scaling experiment is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five training seeds, minimum/mean/maximum training curves, and seed-averaged test results. Figure 2 retains identical minimum-to-maximum shading and reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings in Figure 2 and Tables 1-8 are unchanged. The closing parenthesis added to Table 5 changes neither the parameter values nor the results.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, and their proofs in Appendices B and J are identical, including the additive-rerooter example.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning automated rerooters, online training efficiency, scalability without explicit subgoal reconstruction, and additive-rerooter guarantees.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including heuristic miscalibration, dependence on cluster separation, and explanations of performance under increasing environment complexity.

D1.justification: Appendices C-D retain identical implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and code-access information. No reproducibility details are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography are identical. Positioning relative to earlier rerooting, subgoal-search, and state-space-structure methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page preprint date changes from June 1 to July 21, 2026, and the arXiv stamp updates the version and submission date. The narrative, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 5 repairs the parameter label '(0.60, 1.00' to '(0.60, 1.00)'. This is a small table-formatting correction; figure designs, table structures, and content placement are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates version/date markings and fixes one missing parenthesis in Table 5. These cosmetic edits leave the methods, evidence, proofs, explanations, and reproducibility information unchanged, with no meaningful effect on overall paper quality.
